title: The slot door admits a blog slot on an export and a video slot on an article
instrument: slot.test cases refusing {channel: blog, libraryItemId: video:export:x} and {channel: youtube, libraryItemId: article:r}; then every slot writer enumerated (lib/decision/v1/sources/articleSlot.ts createSlot, app/(studio)/floor/_calendar/real.ts create, packages/kernel/src/slots/import.ts) plus an operator-run count on a store COPY: SELECT count(*) FROM slots WHERE (channel='blog') <> (library_item_id LIKE 'article:%')
evidence: packages/domain/src/slot.ts:94-97 slotItemId export/article prefixes; slotSchema superRefine checks claim/missedAt/publicationId/error/drift only; app/(studio)/floor/_calendar/real.ts:273 refuses a blog slot at ONE writer; packages/kernel/src/slots/schema.ts reads stored rows through the door
body:
## Summary
slotSchema pairs nothing between a slot's channel and the kind of item it names.

## Description
A blog slot publishes by its article approve's pull request (slot.ts header, owner ruling 2026-10-17) and names `article:<runId>`; a video channel uploads an export named `video:export:<id>`. The door (packages/domain/src/slot.ts slotSchema) accepts either item on any channel, so the rule lives only in writers: the Calendar refuses to create a blog slot (app/(studio)/floor/_calendar/real.ts:273) and articleSlot creates only blog+article. A third writer (an import, an agent door) can store a YouTube slot whose item is an article, which the publish tick would try to upload. Fixed: a superRefine pairing channel `blog` with the article prefix and the video channels with the export prefix. Risk 4 because stored rows are read through this door with `must`, so a stored violator turns a read into a throw - the store count must come first.

## Flow
- a writer stores {channel: youtube, libraryItemId: article:r1}
- door admits it
- the publish tick claims it and finds no export (exportIdOf -> undefined)
- fix: refuse at the door, after counting stored violators

## Expected impact
The publish tick can only claim a slot whose item its channel can carry. Could break: reading a stored slot that already violates the pairing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the channel/item pairing held at the door, not at two writers
Before: door admits 2 of 2 mismatched probes (blog+export, youtube+article)
After: 0 of 2 (predicted); stored-row count unknown
Method: probe - the two cases were reasoned against the superRefine; the store count needs a copy only the operator may open
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

body:
## Summary
Two of publication.ts's three metric semantics are ported, tested and read by nothing.

## Description
packages/domain/src/publication.ts keeps StatReel's law as three functions. publicationTotals is read by the Calendar (app/(studio)/floor/_calendar/real.ts:111); groupSums (a group's lower-bound sum) and dailySeries (per-day deltas) have zero consumers outside their own test. They are either a view nobody built (a per-channel or per-day metrics surface) or dead code carrying a mutant. Which one is a product call: the context's description names publications, not a metrics overview.

## Flow
- grep the two exports across app, lib, packages, workers, pipeline
- 0 production readers
- owner decides: build the view (direction) or retire them

## Expected impact
Either the operator gets a metrics rollup the code already computes honestly (lower bounds, null deltas), or ~50 lines and one mutant leave. Nothing breaks either way today.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - whether a ported capability is wanted
Before: 2 exported functions, 0 production readers
After: a direction decision; no figure decides it
Method: probe - the consumer grep was run; the benefit is a product question
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
